articles.title: Eight New Materials from Waste and Living Matter
articles.summary: Researchers have developed eight novel materials using waste and living matter, replacing asbestos and traditional resources. These include fungal‑based composites and recycled industrial by‑products, offering sustainable alternatives for construction and design. The innovations could reduce environmental impact and open new circular‑economy pathways.

articles.title: Grand Ethiopian Dam Sparks Energy‑Water Debate
articles.summary: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam represents a massive engineering and architectural feat, aiming to generate hydropower and address water scarcity. However, it also intensifies regional tensions over water rights and sovereignty. The project highlights the complex trade‑offs between energy development and shared water resources.

articles.title: Casa 9: A‑Frame Retreat Blends Nature and Urban Life
articles.summary: Casa 9 serves as a psychological retreat where indoor and outdoor spaces blend seamlessly for urban families. Its bold A‑frame roof shelters the whole house, creating a fluid connection to the tropical environment. The design dissolves boundaries between occupants, living areas, and nature.

articles.title: Village de Ananti Merges Sea, Forest, and Urban Energy
articles.summary: Village de Ananti is a 392‑room leisure and cultural resort set on a sloping seaside site in Busan. It merges the serenity of ocean and forest with the vibrancy of urban life across 160,324 m². The project offers a balanced blend of recreation, culture, and architectural integration with nature.

articles.title: Casa Cardona Transcends Commercial Architecture
articles.summary: Casa Cardona began as a conventional 165 m² development but evolved into a spatially and culturally significant residence. Its design creates an intimate dialogue with the surrounding desert, transforming the living experience. The project demonstrates how architecture can generate human and cultural value beyond market constraints.

articles.title: Project MMR Features Spiral Staircase and Interior Tree
articles.summary: Project MMR is a house for a young couple featuring unconventional spatial demands and personal symbolism. Highlights include a spiral staircase, an interior‑integrated tree, and visual access to the roof slope from within. The design responds to the owners’ specific lifestyle needs while creating a unique residential experience.

articles.title: Santa Rosa Social Housing Highlights Infrastructure Gaps
articles.summary: Santa Rosa Social Housing addresses Santiago’s growing peripheral settlements caused by rising land prices. Decades of development have left many units disconnected from essential social and technical infrastructure. The project highlights the need for integrated planning and equitable urban expansion.

articles.title: Coqueira House Uses Geometry and Suspended Volume
articles.summary: Coqueira House is organized on two distinct levels, with the upper site accessed via the main road and the lower level carved out as a flat platform. The design features strong geometry, planes, and a suspended volume that contrast with the surrounding topography. The project demonstrates a thoughtful integration of site conditions and architectural form.

articles.title: Ironwood Retreat Capitalizes on Oak Creek's Lush Habitat
articles.summary: Ironwood Retreat is situated along Oak Creek in Sedona, Arizona, where year‑round water flow creates a lush green canopy rare in the region. The wooden structure leverages the site’s natural setting, blending indoor living with the surrounding forest. The project offers a tranquil retreat that capitalizes on the creek’s ecological richness.

articles.title: Dondoh Restaurant Revives Izakaya Spirit in Chile
articles.summary: Dondoh is Chile’s first Japanese grill, recently opened in Santiago, featuring an imposing design inspired by traditional Izakayas. Wood, stone, and fire dominate the interior, creating an atmospheric space for communal dining. The name references an ancient Japanese farmer ceremony, linking culinary tradition with architectural storytelling.

articles.title: MOKUZAI Office Building Combines Timber and Concrete
articles.summary: MOKUZAI is a mixed‑use office building incorporating public health services, featuring a hybrid timber and concrete structure. Designed by IT's Studio, the project showcases sustainable construction methods and modern aesthetics. The design balances durability with environmental considerations, offering flexible workspaces.

articles.title: Palazzo Sogni Revives Florence with Dreamlike Design
articles.summary: Palazzo Sogni revitalizes a centuries‑old palazzo in Florence through restored frescoes and custom furnishings. Designers Elena and Giulia Sella blend historic craftsmanship with contemporary identity, preserving heritage while adding modern flair. The project exemplifies adaptive reuse and the infusion of artisanal skills into historic architecture.

articles.title: Joyce Wang Studio Revisits Hong Kong's Mandarin Oriental
articles.summary: Joyce Wang Studio returns to redesign the Mandarin Oriental The Landmark in Hong Kong after a decade. The new iteration draws inspiration from Hong Kong's architecture, landscape, and rich history to create a refined hospitality experience.

articles.title: Narwal's Flow 2 White Reimagines Robot Vacuum Design
articles.summary: Narwal introduces a refined white finish for its Flow 2 robot vacuum with subtle lighting and a cohesive docking station. The design presents a more thoughtful approach to integrating home technology into domestic spaces.

articles.title: Crocs x BARK Launches $100 Giant Clog Dog Bed
articles.summary: Crocs collaborates with BARK to create an oversized orange Croc that doubles as a functional dog bed. The whimsical design tests brand dedication while serving a practical pet care purpose.

articles.title: Lenovo Unveils Color Ink Tablet with Black and White Display
articles.summary: Lenovo announces the Xiaoxin 10.1 Color Ink tablet featuring a unique approach to e-ink technology. Despite its name, the device switches from full color LCD to black and white display, offering a different reading experience.

articles.title: Duramobi's Underwater Speaker Transforms Pool Spaces
articles.summary: Duramobi releases an underwater Bluetooth speaker designed to turn swimming pools into immersive sound systems. The device addresses the need for waterproof audio solutions in outdoor recreational settings.

articles.title: AWOL Valerion Enhances NFL Viewing with Advanced Picture Control
articles.summary: AWOL introduces the Valerion projector system designed for immersive big-screen sports viewing. The product emphasizes enhanced picture control options for optimal home entertainment during major sporting events.

articles.title: Compact Yukon Cabin Fits King Bed Without Loft
articles.summary: Zook Cabins presents the 296-square-foot Yukon Park Model that accommodates a king-size bed on the main floor without requiring a loft. The design maximizes space efficiency while maintaining residential comfort for temporary living.

articles.title: Even Realities Debuts Elegant Tortoise Shell Smart Glasses
articles.summary: Even Realities launches new smart glasses featuring a stunning tortoise shell frame design. The aesthetic focus positions the product as a premium wearable that prioritizes fashion alongside functionality.

articles.title: Apple's iPad Mini Challenges High-End iPhone Pricing
articles.summary: Apple releases a $699 iPad mini that makes the $1,999 iPhone Duo less compelling as a purchase. The new tablet offers strong value proposition while competing with Apple's own premium smartphone lineup.

articles.title: 28-Foot Tiny Home Features Living Room in Staircase
articles.summary: The Wildscape tiny home incorporates a multi-functional staircase that serves as a living room area. Terraced timber seating provides lounge space, storage, and vertical circulation in an efficient 28-foot design.

articles.title: 8bitdo Honors Tomb Raider with Nostalgic Gaming Controllers
articles.summary: 8bitdo celebrates 30 years of Tomb Raider with two specially designed controllers for nostalgic gamers. The products appeal to fans who want to revisit classic gaming experiences.

articles.title: Minisforum N5 Air 7640 Features Upgradeable Slide-Out Motherboard
articles.summary: Minisforum introduces the N5 Air 7640 mini PC with a slide-out motherboard design enabling easy upgrades. The innovative approach addresses storage limitations and future-proofing needs for compact computing solutions.

articles.title: Hanger's Hidden Trick Turns Question Into Exclamation
articles.summary: A closet full of clothes can leave you unsure which shirt fits best. This hanger design solves that problem with a clever hidden feature.

articles.title: Logitech Pebble Up Mouse Transforms Vertically
articles.summary: Logitech's new mouse offers a vertical configuration for power users who need more space. The design adapts to different workstation setups.

articles.title: NUS Researchers Create Touchscreen Sleeve with Electronic Threads
articles.summary: Researchers at NUS developed a sleeve that turns a sleeve into a touchscreen. The electronic threads enable interactive touch without a separate device.

articles.title: DeWalt Tool Batteries Charge Laptops Without Outlet
articles.summary: DeWalt's drill batteries can now charge laptops directly. This innovation eliminates the need for separate power adapters.

articles.title: Lamp That Refuses to Need Outlet or Charger
articles.summary: A lamp design that operates without traditional power sources. It reimagines how lighting can be used in portable settings.

articles.title: Statik PowerStand Turns USB-C Cable into Phone Stand
articles.summary: Statik's PowerStand repurposes a USB-C cable as a folding phone stand. It provides a stable surface for charging and viewing.

articles.title: Reclaimed Timber Frames Shape Coastal Sauna and Hub
articles.summary: An arctic sauna and community hub built from reclaimed timber portal frames. The design showcases sustainable construction in Norway.

articles.title: Fictional Beverage Campaign Raises Fake News Awareness
articles.summary: A fictional drink campaign warns about misinformation in Paris and NYC. The project combines art with media literacy education.

articles.title: Jorge Diego Etienne Exhibits 15 Years of Design Prototypes
articles.summary: The designer's museum exhibition reveals nearly 15 years of sketches and prototypes. It showcases his long-term design practice.

articles.title: MOLD Greek Island Residence with Seven Open-Air Courtyards
articles.summary: A rose-colored home on Serifos features seven courtyards and curved passages. The design integrates nature and architecture on a Greek island.

articles.title: Aron Sanchez-Baranda Finds Otherworldly Forms in Marine Life
articles.summary: An artist explores nonhuman life forms through sculpture and design. The work invites viewers to reconsider perception of marine organisms.

articles.title: Ergonomic Chess Set with Tactile Contours and Weighted Bases
articles.summary: Lucy Aboonour's chess set uses wood and walnut with ergonomic features. The design optimizes tactile recognition and playability.

articles.title: Rima Dain Launches Custom Architectural Outdoor Rugs
articles.summary: Marbella-based studio Rima Dain creates custom outdoor rugs using UV-stabilized synthetic flatweaves and water-permeable backings. These architectural pieces frame exterior living zones for residential and hospitality terraces. The designs combine durability with functional zoning capabilities.

articles.title: Washable Electronic Fibers Turn Sleeve Into Touchscreen
articles.summary: New electronic fiber technology embeds touchscreen functionality into fabric sleeves that survive machine washing. The material can display images and video, respond to finger presses, and connect wirelessly to digital devices. It remains breathable and flexible like everyday fabric.

articles.title: Architect Reimagines Design Beyond Human-Centered Perspectives
articles.summary: Architect Ariel André explores how shifting design perspectives toward animals and other non-human life forms can reshape inhabited spaces. The guest essay challenges anthropocentric approaches to architecture and urban design. It proposes new frameworks for designing with overlooked bodies and ecosystems in mind.

articles.title: Sagmeister Exhibition Uses Data to Show Global Progress
articles.summary: Stefan Sagmeister's Finally, Something Good exhibition at La Gaîté Lyrique reframes global metrics across health, democracy, and equality. The data-driven artworks invite visitors to view the current era through optimism rather than cynicism. The show transforms statistical information into compelling visual narratives.

articles.title: October 2026’s Best New Typefaces Revealed
articles.summary: Creative Boom rounds up the best new typefaces released in October 2026. The selection includes an industrial slab named after a hardness scale and a display face inspired by lace. The list highlights fresh typography options for designers.

articles.title: Photo Book Documents Soviet-Era Socialist Hotel Architecture
articles.summary: A new photo book documents the hospitality architecture of the Soviet era behind the Iron Curtain. The collection showcases concrete hotel designs from the socialist period. It offers a visual retrospective of Eastern Bloc accommodation architecture.

articles.title: Artist Creates Playful Artphabet Featuring Famous Painters
articles.summary: César Cid has created an Artphabet featuring 26 notable artists abstracted into letterforms. The playful series demonstrates how recognizable paintings can be transformed into abstract typography. The project blends art history with graphic design experimentation.

articles.title: A Good Idea for a Lamp for Ferrari Fanatics
articles.summary: This vintage desk lamp is by VEB Zweckleuchtenbau, a state-owned East German lamp manufacturer of the 1970s. It's a pretty basic Communist-era design, with no mistaking where the switch is. You can adjust the lamp's tilt by moving the stalk in the little channel in the base. Which makes me think: If you took a vintage Ferrari shift gate, and made a lamp like this with a more Ferrari-esque shade, I bet you could sell it for an absurd amount of money.

articles.title: Drawing with Absurdly Long Pencils
articles.summary: Scenic artist Nikolay Laukhin creates large-scale backdrops for the Mariinsky Theater in St. Petersburg. And I mean seriously large-scale: You might wonder how many levels of scaffolds he has to erect in order to paint one of those pieces. The answer is, none. Here's how he and his team do the work: I remember a Foundation Year exercise where they had us draw with a pencil on a stick, but it wasn't that long! Laukhin's got lots of behind-the-scenes footage here .

articles.title: Improvised Tools: A Creative "Juggad" Leak Detector
articles.summary: An innovative improvised method for detecting tire leaks using available materials instead of traditional tools. The jugaad concept encourages resourceful engineering when equipment is lacking.

articles.summary: Chilean studio Paralelo Transversal has designed a rectangular house with a large hip roof and a terrace that cantilevers over a ravine in Puerto Varas, Chile. articles.summary: Antaira has introduced the LanoSync Q-Series industrial network switches. The devices combine precision timing with rugged reliability for industrial environments.

articles.title: Keene Named Industry Legend at Self-Driving Awards
articles.summary: Kenilworth’s Keene has been named an Industry Legend at the Self-Driving Industry Awards. Aurrigo also won two titles at the same event.

articles.title: Miyamoto to Receive Japanese Honour
articles.summary: Shigeru Miyamoto, the legendary Nintendo game designer, is set to receive a Japanese honour. The recognition celebrates his extensive contributions to video game design.

articles.title: Etienne Prototype Exhibition at Museo Franz Mayer
articles.summary: A decade-long prototype journey by Jorge Diego Etienne is being showcased at Museo Franz Mayer. The exhibition highlights his iterative design process and innovative concepts.

articles.summary: FrogBox has won an Australian Good Design Award for its sports camera. The award recognizes the product’s innovative design and functionality.

articles.summary: The longlist for the Archiproducts Design Awards 2026 has been revealed. It includes a diverse range of products and designs from around the world.

articles.summary: Winning designers at the Archiproducts Design Awards will receive a Verde Antico marble trophy. The trophy symbolizes excellence in product design.
